text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> devon: P1 alert: multiple parse-engine preproc pods in us-west-2 are being OOMKilled; pod restart loops observed and ~5% 5xx rate on /v1/prompt. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/preproc-cpu-oom> :rotating_light:

devon: I'm oncall, jumping in. pulling logs now. pinging maya for recent changes.

maya: no infra deploys in the last hour. we did ship a tokenizer micro-optimization last night behind a feature flag, only canary. looks like a prompt-pattern spike from a customer subset.

devon: getting pod list and descriptions
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep parse-engine
parse-engine-5f7b8   2/2 Running  3 (OOMKilled)  10m
parse-engine-6c9d0   1/2 CrashLoopBackOff  5 (OOMKilled)  8m
```

devon: sample pod logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] token_parse_worker: Alloc failed, requested 134217728 bytes
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Killed
```

ops-bot: Noting a single GPU node reported a CUDA error earlier: cudaErrorIllegalAddress in decode path on node ip-10-0-4-32, but majority of failures are CPU OOM in preproc containers.

maya: likely heavy nested regex / eager tokenization on some inputs. we should throttle heavy prompts and fall back to simple tokenizer path.

devon: current mitigation plan: 1) scale parse-engine replicas to 1 to reduce concurrent preproc load, 2) enable request-level rate limit for legacy customers, 3) route new traffic to fallback model variant. executing step 1 now.

devon: `kubectl scale deployment/parse-engine --replicas=1 -n inference`

nina: CS update: two customers submitted errors (acme, beta-co), both saw 502/timeout in last 10m. notifying affected accounts and offering status page link.

liam: I'll take the lead on the runtime fix. proposed hotfix: disable complex tokenizer code path via env override (TOKENIZER_COMPLEX=false) and restart pods sequentially. canary first.

liam: `kubectl set env deploy/parse-engine TOKENIZER_COMPLEX=false -n inference && kubectl rollout restart deploy/parse-engine -n inference --record`

liam: canary pod is up. monitoring logs — no OOM in the canary after 90s, CPU usage down ~65% from baseline.

ops-bot: metrics: /v1/prompt 5xx rate decreased from 5.1% to 1.2% after canary; p95 latency improved.

devon: good. keep replicas at 1 until we validate for 20m, then incrementally scale. preserving node cordon on the GPU node that had cuda error until we confirm it's unrelated.

nina: CS will send a short timeline to affected customers and update the status page. will queue follow-up with impact details (error counts, window, apis affected).

devon: documenting actions in incident doc: https://redwood/incidents/1754302468. marking current state = mitigated (customer-impacting). handing off to liam for ongoing monitoring and rollback authority.

liam: acknowledged. I'll keep the runbook open and run nightly regression checks on tokenizer change. plan: leave TOKENIZER_COMPLEX=false for 2h, then attempt controlled re-enable with a throttled feature flag.

maya: create a postmortem checklist: reproduce spike with synthetic prompts, add prefilter to reject extremely large nested regex inputs, add CPU OOM alerting with per-container thresholds, and add tokenization timeouts.

devon: oncall handoff -> liam. status at handoff: mitigated, P1, customer-impacting, active escalation open. next update in 20m or on major change.

incident-bot: Incident update: Owner=liam, Status=Mitigated, Severity=P1, StartTs=1754302468.

liam: taking over monitoring and postmortem. will post full timeline and action items once stable.

nina: thanks all — CS will follow up with customers and keep this thread updated for notes to include in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
